extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Navy public affairs officers, commanders, CHINFO field activities, and contracted public affairs/communications personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Official SECNAV instruction setting Department of the Navy public affairs policy, information-release rules, roles/responsibilities, media relations, print/visual/web standards, and operational security constraints for PA activities. Intended to govern how PAOs and commands produce and release information to internal and external audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Mandate and Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of Department of Navy (DON) public affairs efforts is to provide strategic counsel, operational planning and tactical execution of communication as a function of national objectives, joint combat operations and the naval mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs is a command function applicable throughout DON; PA activities support deterrence, prevention, response, and the joint warfighter. DOD public affairs doctrine (e.g., DODD 5400.13, Joint Pub 3-61) applies; authority for DON public affairs comes from the Secretary of the Navy. Commands must recognize public affairs as essential to mission accomplishment and provide timely, accurate information consistent with security and privacy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Disclosure (Public Affairs Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Full Disclosure. For a government founded on the principle of an empowered public, the default position is full and prompt disclosure. Withholding must be the exception, and justified for specific and legally defensible reasons. Potential embarrassment is not a justification to withhold information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release unless precluded by valid security classifications or statute. Delays and withholding for embarrassment undermine public trust. See supplemental guidance for complete description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expeditious Release (Public Affairs Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Expeditious Release. Information should be released as expeditiously as practical, and from the lowest possible level, consistent with release policies and required reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All DON members are communicators and should commit to full and expeditious release appropriate to their level. See Chapter 2 for required reviews. Accident and incident releases: within one hour of command awareness of event (timeliness requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics (Public Affairs Principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ethics. DON holds itself to a high ethical standard. In dealings with the public, DON must adhere rigorously to such a standard because a loss of public confidence can undermine DON's ability to complete its mission."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid distortion, propaganda, or use of information to shield government from criticism. Adhere to DOD ethics resources and guidance (links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Accuracy is a Responsibility and a Requirement. Distorting the facts or publishing inaccurate information... creates a sense of mistrust... and damages DON credibility... It will not be allowed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must ensure releases are fact-checked. Web content must be accurate and current ("Power of the Internet"). Inadvertent inaccuracies should be corrected promptly and transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Timeliness is a Responsibility and a Requirement. DON PA activities will practice maximum disclosure with minimum delay."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accident/incident releases: made within one hour of command awareness. Consider perishability of tactical/operational information when deciding release timing (e.g., departures/arrivals).

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Principles of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD principles: make information fully and readily available consistent with statute; free flow of general and military information without censorship or propaganda; do not classify or withhold to avoid criticism; withhold when disclosure would harm national security, safety/privacy, or be contrary to law; detailed PA planning may be required for major programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these principles in all PA planning and align DON releases to these tenets. Propaganda has no place in DOD public affairs programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Request Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A FOIA request must be in writing, cite or imply FOIA, reasonably describe the records sought so a knowledgeable official can conduct a search with reasonable effort, and if fees apply, indicate willingness to pay or request a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request lacks these elements, advise and assist the requester in perfecting it. Media queries that are releasable may be answered without formal FOIA. If in doubt, consult the FOIA authority. See www.foia.navy.mil for FOIA guidance and reading room.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Responsibilities and Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA responsibilities should be assigned to non-public affairs personnel when possible to provide check-and-balance; PAOs should be familiar with FOIA elements and must forward FOIA requests to the cognizant FOIA authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should accept FOIA requests sent to them and forward appropriately. Release information releasable under FOIA without requiring a FOIA request if that serves efficiency and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Disclosure Presumption and Exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Disclosure should be the rule, not the exception... The burden is on the government to justify withholding of a document..." FOIA contains specific exemptions that may preclude release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must consider whether requested information is releasable under FOIA and consult FOIA authority when doubts exist. Familiarize with common exemptions and appeals process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act Collection and Use Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may collect only such personal information that is relevant and necessary to carry out a purpose required by statute or executive order; personal information collected for one purpose cannot be used for another without consent; provide the four-point Privacy Act statement when collecting personal info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must limit collection to necessary information (e.g., visitors, contributors). Publish routine uses of records and obtain written consent for other uses or transfers absent a statutory exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act Safeguards and Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish administrative, technical and physical safeguards for records, rules of conduct, and training; individuals have the right to see records about themselves and to challenge accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure training on the Privacy Act for PA and editorial staff; limit use of social security numbers; coordinate with legal/privacy office when handling personal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act Exceptions and Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Privacy Act permits release of personal information without consent under specified exceptions (12 conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should consult the Navy Privacy Act instruction and legal advisors to determine applicability of exceptions before disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing Test for Privacy vs Public Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA and the Privacy Act require balancing individual privacy interests against public right to government information; factors include whether info is well-known, public-domain, practical obscurity, sensitivity of allegations, status of individual (high-level official vs lower-level), death of individual, and whether disclosure would endanger personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider listed factors (a–k) when weighing disclosure: e.g., federal employees' basic data have no expectation of privacy; high-level officials have diminished privacy; unproven allegations may not outweigh privacy interest. Consult legal counsel as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and Policy Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: All commanders will ensure PAOs have adequate clearance and access; activities must review material prepared for release to ensure it reveals no classified or sensitive unclassified information; certain categories must be submitted for higher policy/security review (CHINFO, DIRPA, CNO N09N2, Marine Corps INT C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow submission procedures after command/chain-of-command review. Voluntary review is available for sources outside DOD. See supplemental guidance for categories requiring review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified Information Protection and Release
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs must ensure information is fully coordinated and properly classified until approved for release; classified information is generally not given to reporters; rare access requires specific approvals (JFC, CHINFO, OASD(PA)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reporter or photographer has wrongful access, immediately contact Security Manager; PA personnel must not comment on classified info; Security Manager will coordinate further action (may request deletion, etc.). Follow SECNAVINST 5510.36 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions for Inadvertent Disclosure of Classified Material
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reporter/photographer has been given wrongful access, the PAO must contact the command Security Manager immediately and refrain from statements regarding the classified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security Manager notifies CNO (N09N2) who will coordinate action. Options include requesting deletion or taking no action to avoid confirming existence. Do not comment publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational Security (OPSEC) — Releasable Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on generally releasable OPSEC items: confirmation of ships/aircraft plainly visible, approximate size of friendly forces (not exact numbers), casualty figures (names withheld until next-of-kin notification), results of completed missions, types and general amounts of ordnance, number of aerial combat missions flown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines apply unless otherwise specified by PAG or higher operational authority. Confirm the obvious but avoid detailing sensitive specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational Security (OPSEC) — Non-Releasable Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally non-releasable: future plans/operations; detailed vulnerabilities/weaknesses; rules of engagement; security measures/force protection/deceptive actions; intelligence collection activities; information about downed aircraft/ships during planning/rescue; specific types of ordnance and methods; locations/activities of special operations forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release unless declared releasable by applicable PAG or higher authority, or declassified. Coordinate with operational/security authorities for ambiguous items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Classified Aspects of Equipment/Procedures/Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classified aspects of equipment, procedures and operations must be protected from disclosure because of jeopardy to future operations, risk to life, host-nation/allied sensitivities, or disclosure of intelligence methods and sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these guidelines to inform what military personnel may say to media and to set ground rules for media coverage. Consult security officers for gray areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit Departures and Arrivals — Timeliness Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ship and unit departures and arrivals are generally releasable on or near the date; information at tactical/operational levels is perishable and decisions about release must reflect perishability and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public interest and OPSEC; commanders must consider how quickly information becomes outdated and the associated operational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs Organization — Channels of Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: SECNAV establishes DON public affairs policy; CNO, CMC and senior commanders implement it; CHINFO is delegated responsibility for coordinating, planning and implementing PA policy and programs and acts as DON public spokesperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA authority flows from SECNAV through CHINFO; commanders are responsible for implementation; field activities communicate regionally and nationally. See supplemental guidance for CHINFO field activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHINFO Roles and Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: CHINFO acts as DON public spokesperson; advises SECNAV/CNO on PA policy; coordinates/evaluates information of national/international interest for release; originates/disseminates Navy developments; provides community relations/internal information guidance; approves contracted PA support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHINFO may issue subsequent changes to regulations; PAOs and commands must coordinate with CHINFO for policy review/clearance where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAO Chain-of-Command and Command Function
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs is a command function; subject to senior authority, each officer exercising command authority is responsible for PA--internal information, public information/community relations and planning within that command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs will report to the commander/commanding officer for PA issues. Capability varies by echelon; commands must resource PA appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs and Collateral Duty Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs officers shall not be assigned collateral duties that have the potential to conflict or impede with their primary responsibility as command spokespersons (e.g., being investigating officer in a mishap would compromise spokesperson role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assignments that create conflicts of interest or disqualify PAOs from being official spokespersons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted Public Affairs Personnel Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracted public affairs and communications management personnel are not authorized to act as official Navy spokespersons and cannot operate a publicly available website unless a Navy official with authority for public release controls the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors may provide support but official releases and website content control must reside with Navy officials. Contracts should reflect this and CHINFO approves requests for contracted PA support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery Forwarding and Distribution (JCCC/NVNS)
rubrics_metrics.description: By DOD and Navy policy, the single point to forward imagery of immediate interest is Joint Combat Camera Center (JCCC); digital files with the VIRIN sent to JCCC are automatically sent to NVNS which uploads to Navy NewsStand and markets to external media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should ensure Fleet imagery needed by Naval Media Center, NVNS, historians, and other consumers is forwarded through JCCC via correct file naming and FTP procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery Alteration Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Alteration of official U.S. Navy imagery is prohibited except for specified techniques: darkroom/digital adjustments (dodging, burning, color balancing, spotting, contrast adjustment) that achieve accurate recording; enhancement for technical purposes if not misrepresenting the subject; obvious masking for security/legal/privacy; cropping/editing/enlargement not considered alteration unless they misrepresent facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-production effects for dramatic/narrative use are authorized only if they do not misrepresent the subject or are clearly apparent as non-accurate. Digital conversion/compression is authorized. Misrepresentation is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Information (V/I) Mission and Role
rubrics_metrics.description: V/I products tell and promote the Navy story to policy-makers, media, and the American people; imagery documents Sailors/Marines, operations, and historic events and supports legal, medical, training, and historical needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V/I and COMCAM provide VIDOC, OPDOC, TECDOC, and support shipboard/shore V/I support centers. Manage V/I assets to serve internal and external audiences and records retention needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: V/I Program Management Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The CNO’s Assistant for Naval Media (N09C1) manages the V/I and COMCAM Program; each Navy Budget Submitting Office has a V/I Management Officer responsible for budgeting/oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SECNAVINST 3104.1 and OPNAVINST 3104.3 for specific V/I function responsibilities and program management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command Newspapers — Editorial and Content Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Military newspapers shall avoid labor union news that may provoke controversy (editorial endorsements, criticism of union actions), shall not publish material implying Service/DOD endorsement of a commercial product or service, shall not glamorize alcohol or tobacco, and editorial copy prepared by a command is primarily for internal audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club activity coverage may emphasize activities not beverages; internal material requested by outside publishers should be referred to FOIA office; maintain credits and not imply contractor employment in CE papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper Masthead and Disclaimer Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The masthead of all funded and CE newspapers must contain commander name, newspaper name and producing command; include statement: 'The editorial content of this newspaper is edited and approved by the public affairs office of (command).'; include authorization-type disclaimers for CE papers about advertising not constituting DOD endorsement and authorized-publication disclaimer informing that contents do not necessarily reflect official views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masthead and disclaimers must be in type no smaller than six-point as specified; CE contractor credits must not imply DOD employment. Include equal-opportunity and advertising availability statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper Distribution and Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded newspapers may be distributed through official channels and must send specified copies to Marine Corps/Navy headquarters and AFIS; commands must conduct readership surveys every two years and after major editorial/stylistic changes and report results to readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CE contracts should require independent contractor readership surveys; appropriated funds/manpower may be used for distribution where authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-based Newspapers and Online Versions
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO may require publisher of a funded or CE newspaper to provide an online version; production of online version does not violate internal hosting requirements if CE publisher contractually bears production/circulation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DODI 5120.4 and related guidance on electronic newspapers; ensure contractual terms cover online publication responsibilities and disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Bulletins and Summaries Authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications comprising excerpts from approved national and international news and opinion sources are authorized for deployed or isolated commands, provided the publication includes appropriate disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such digests must carry appropriate disclaimers and follow Article 1002 and supplemental guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Websites — Authority and PAO Role
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of a command public website remains a command prerogative consistent with leadership responsibilities for public communication; management and oversight of all content on a publicly accessible website is the responsibility of the PAO acting for the commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For access-restricted sites different concerns apply; PAOs must be aware of benefits/pitfalls of public web sites. Contracted public affairs cannot operate public sites unless a Navy official controls content. See SECNAVINST 5720.47 and supplemental guidance for detailed standards and security concerns.
